notes: The Hebrew doubles nasi ehad distributively and the ASV writes it once with a distributive every; the repeated noun is unrepresented and the second numeral takes the every (rules 22, 41).

Competing reading on the every: treat both members of the second nasi ehad as unrepresented under rule 22 and give the every to matteh as a supplied quantifying determiner under rule 15. The accepted reading is preferred because rule 41 records ehad as a morpheme that licenses a distributive each or every, and rule 15 gives such a determiner to the bare noun only where no morpheme in the clause licenses it.
linhol is rendered divide ... for inheritance and headed on the complement (rule 44), the alternative heading on divide.
